preview: Software Developer interview experience at BNY Mellon for the 2024 FTE role, detailing the online assessment, technical rounds, and hiring manager round.
content: Software Developer Interview Experience PRADEEP BHANDARI l B.Tech ELECTRONICS 2021 - 2024 FOR FTE 2024 17th August 2023 BNY Mellon came to our campus to recruit final-year students for an FTE position as a software developer. There were around 150+ applicants. Eligibility: 7.5 CGPA Criteria Branches Allowed: CS, IT, ExTC, Electronics, Electrical, and Mechanical. Round 1 - Online Assessment (10th August 2023) Online Test conducted on Hackerrank Platform having 4 DSA Questions to be completed within 120 Minutes. 1. Binary Storage (Easy) - You’re given a binary 2D array of size NxM, each row of the matrix has some value x denoting the xth bit of the current number is set. Consider arr[] = {3,2,1} meaning the number would be 1110 which is equivalent to 14, similarly, other N rows would contribute some value you have to sort in descending order of values and return the indices according to row number. Eg - bitArrays = [[0,2],[2,3],[2,1]] index binary decimal 0 0101 5 1 1100 12 2 0110 6 here, the values in order of descending are [12,6,5] so, we return [1,2,0]. I was able to solve this completely. 2. Merge Sort Counts (Medium) - This problem was a variation of Count Inversion Problem based on merge sort. 3. Valid Keys(Medium) - Can’t recall the question, but I was able to solve this completely. 4. Array Compromise (Hard)- Can’t recall the exact question but it was something like this, an array is considered to be compromised if the bitwise OR of all elements in the subarray is present in the array itself and we have to find all the compromised array. I was able to solve one medium and one easy question completely and for the other medium 4/15 test cases were passed and for hard 9/15 test cases were passed. 19 students were shortlisted for the interviews, but later on, 6 more were shortlisted. All the interviews were conducted in person. Technical Round 1 (50 mins) 1. The interviewer was not that friendly and he asked for my resume and started going through it. After going through my resume for a few minutes, he asked the very famous “Tell me about yourself ?” 2. Then he asked which all programming languages I know? (I said C++,Python and JS) 3. Then he asked me to rank myself in each language based on Proficiency. 4. As I mentioned that I am proficient in C++, he went ahead and asked whether I know about OOPS? 5. Then he asked, what are the different concepts in OOPS?(I explained 4 pillars of OOPS) 6. Asked me in detail about Inheritance and also asked to write the code. 7. We had a discussion about various types of Inheritance and why we need to use Inheritance. 8. Now, he asked me to explain Polymorphism. (Tip: Don’t tell a bookish definition, it makes a bad impression, try to explain with examples and by relating it with the real world.) 9. We had a long discussion about Early binding and late Binding. He went deep into overriding and also asked me to write code and tell the output for multiple cases. 10. He asked me whether I know Data Structures and Algorithms. I said yes. 11. Now, he asked me to write all the data structures I am familiar with. (I forgot to mention Linked List) 12. He asked me to explain mutable and immutable data structures. 13. He asked me whether I am familiar with Linked List (both singly and doubly linked list). 14. He asked me two DSA questions based on Linked List. a. Reverse a linked list b. Insert a node in the linked list given its position. (Tip: Practice writing code on paper at home, here I was asked to write code on paper. ) 15. He asked me whether I am familiar with Python or not? 16. He started asking me about python data types and also asked me to write code for declaring them and iterating through them. 17. He asked me the difference between list and tuples. 18. He asked me whether I know List Comprehension or not? 19. Asked me to write a class in Python. (PS. I told him that I don’t remember the exact syntax) 20. Lastly, the interviewer asked If I had any questions. (PS. Always ask 1-2 questions that show that you’re interested in the company as well as you get to know about the company and the work they do and their tech stack) 21. Finally, the interviewer greeted me with a handshake and wished me luck. 6 students were eliminated after this round. We were informed by the mail that we are selected for the second round. Technical Round 2 (40 mins) 1. This round too started with the famous “Tell me about yourself?” 2. This time the interviewer was very friendly. 3. He went through my resume and told me that he is impressed by my CGPA. 4. Now, he asked me whether I am familiar with Data Structures & Algorithms, I of course said YES! 5. Now he started asking me questions and asked me to explain the approach and then write the code on paper. 6. First question: Given a decimal number, convert it into binary and return a string. ( I took 2-3 examples for dry run and explained the approach to the interviewer, he was satisfied with the approach and asked me to write the code) 7. Second question: Given an array of integers, return the first repeating integer. ( I gave him 2 approaches to solve this problem, each with improved time complexity, and he was satisfied with all of them and asked not to write the code.) 8. Third question: Merge sort (In this, he first asked me if I knew about merge sort. Then he asked me to explain the algorithm in detail. Asked about the time complexity and use cases and after the entire discussion he asked me to write the code on paper.) 9. Now the interviewer said that's all from his side and asked me whether I have questions for him? 10. I asked 2 questions and he answered them very nicely. This round was all about DSA questions and problem solving. After 10-15 mins I got mail for the HR round. Hiring Manager Round (25 mins) 1. The interviewer was very friendly and he made me comfortable by asking questions like how was your day, how are you feeling, and how much you enjoyed the process. 2. He went through my resume and praised me for my CPI. 3. Again the most famous question, “Tell me about yourself?” 4. Why BNY Mellon? 5. He asked me, how did I manage a good CPI along with coding and CS subjects? 6. Why Software Engineering being from an Electronics Background?( we had a very long discussion in this question ) 7. Why did you choose Electronics Engineering at VJTI, instead of taking Computer Science in other colleges in Mumbai? 8. Now he asked about my family background? 9. He asked me about my internship experience in TCS ( Again had a long discussion regarding the internship) 10. He asked to talk about one recent failure. 11. Asked me to tell one situation where I struggled a lot and how I managed to conquer it? 12. He asked till now you had a driving factor of getting a job as SDE for learning and preparing. Now if you get the opportunity what thing will drive you to continue working and learning? 13. Now he went to my hackerrank test scores and asked me to justify the low score in the hard question as I was able to pass only 9/15 test cases. ( I justified it by telling that I was not able to do it completely due to time constraint as I gave more time to medium questions, he seemed satisfied with the answer) 14. The interviewer asked if I had any questions, I asked one. (TIP: Always be honest and try to answer the questions such that it follows the company's core values and it is always good to study about the company before appearing for the interview.) On that same day, at 9:55 PM, the results were released. 12 students were chosen, and I was one of them😊. Tips: 1. Make sure you enter with a smile and greet them because your first impression can have a lot of impact. 2. Maintain a grooming standard in the interviews, because it impacts your body language. 3. Stay calm, composed, and confident while speaking. 4. Prepare the “Tell me about yourself” and a few common HR questions beforehand. 5. For a DSA Question, try to think out loud and share your ideas with the interviewer. 6. If you finished writing your code, make sure to dry-run it before presenting it to the interviewer. 7. Try to maintain a smile on your face throughout the interview, that reflects how much confidence you have. 8. Don’t lose hope in rejection. Your rejections are just a redirection. Resources (That I followed) ●DSA: Striver’s SDE Sheet, CodeHelp DSA Course, takeUForward ●OOPS: OOPS Roadmap - Love Babbar, OOPS Interviewbit FAQs ●DBMS: DBMS Roadmap - Love Babbar, CodeHelp DBMS Playlist ●OS: OS Roadmap - Love Babbar, OS Interviewbit FAQs ●SQL: CodeHelp SQL One Shot, W3Schools SQL Exercises ●Aptitude: Indiabix, PrepInsta ●Puzzles: GFG Puzzles “Remember, every interview is a chance to grow, learn, and shine brighter in your next opportunity.” ALL THE BEST👍 PS. For any help, feel free to reach out to me here.
